Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has backed Kylian Mbappé over the controversy surrounding the forward’s remarks about China, saying both the player and the club responded with class and had done what was required to address the issue. Mourinho said he felt represented by the reactions of Mbappé and Real Madrid, adding that the club had no further role to play in the matter after issuing an apology to the Chinese people. Speaking at a press conference on Saturday ahead of Real Madrid’s visit to Racing Santander, the Portuguese manager said the incident reflected the risks of making public comments in an increasingly sensitive world. “With this situation involving China, these are the dangers of today’s world, where many times the best thing you can do is keep your mouth shut, because there’s danger in so many things you say or comment on,” Mourinho told reporters. He, however, praised the responses of the French forward and the Spanish club, saying their swift reactions demonstrated responsibility. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Both have had the class to have an immediate reaction, and I feel as a coach very represented by my club and by my player,” he said. Mourinho added that he had seen a strong sense of responsibility from the club and believed the matter had been adequately addressed. “I’ve seen a lot of responsibility from a club which, at this level, is a club of great class, and as far as we’re concerned, that’s it, we’ve done our part, there’s nothing more for us to do,” he said. The controversy followed comments by Mbappé about an internet meme featuring his face superimposed on that of former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. The remarks drew criticism in China, prompting the player, Real Madrid and La Liga to issue apologies. Mourinho also spoke in defence of Mbappé’s character, describing the 27-year-old as intelligent and mature, while praising the way he handled finishing behind Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane in the Ballon d’Or voting. “Kylian is very intelligent, very mature, with a very high level of self-esteem,” Mourinho said. “At the same time, he shows real class in the way he’s interpreted the Ballon d’Or going to Harry. In him I’ve only seen and felt class and respect. “One thing is knowing you’re the best, and another is having respect for those who have also done a lot to win a trophy. From him I only see class.” Kane was named the winner of the award ahead of Mbappé, who finished second, while Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham placed 11th. Mourinho said he was pleased for Kane, whom he coached at Tottenham Hotspur, despite his disappointment that his current player did not win the award. “I had the privilege of working with Harry, he’s a great player and a great professional and a great person,” he said. “Inside the frustration that my player (Mbappé) didn’t win, well, I have to be honest and say I’m very happy for Harry, a player and a boy who deserves it.” The Real Madrid manager also expressed surprise at Bellingham’s position in the voting, saying the midfielder’s 11th-place finish had left him astonished. “What left me with my mouth open in surprise was Jude Bellingham 11th, no comments,” he said.
